  • You prefer highly defined, static playbooks and feel uncomfortable operating in ambiguity or helping to build the motion as you go.

  • You are not motivated by digging into the details of financial models, customer data and assumptions to create credible, defensible analysis.

  • You find it difficult to challenge or influence senior stakeholders, or you avoid direct collaboration with Sales on commercial outcomes.

Equity: We offer equity across all roles at hx, making it a significant component of total compensation. Your Talent Partner will be able to share more details about this.

  • Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together.

Lead Product Designer

📍 Manchester (Hybrid, up to 4 days WFH)

💰 £70k-£90k (negotiable)

Street Group is one of the fastest-growing PropTech companies in the UK. We want to be the leading creator of delightful experiences for everybody involved in buying, selling, renting and letting property, regardless of their involvement, to improve the industry for everybody by elevating UK Estate Agencies through world-class technology.

We're now looking for a Lead Product Designer - the most senior individual contributor for design within a product domain. This is predominantly an IC role: you'll set the design bar for an entire domain through the quality of your own work, the patterns you contribute, and the way you raise the designers around you. We're flexible on this for the right person, if you've got management experience, or want to line-manage one or two designers alongside the IC work, let's talk.

We want someone who is tired of the "feature factory" grind, who is past needing to be told what's worth working on, and who is ready to set the design direction for a domain in one of the most exciting PropTech companies in the UK.

If you look at most UX job ads, you see a laundry list of requirements. We prefer to tell you how we actually operate so you can decide if this is the right environment for you.

  • At Street Group, design is a strategic seat. Lead Product Designers drive roadmap conversations alongside their product and engineering counterparts, not respond to them.

  • Our users rely on us to run their businesses, so they love talking to us. You can spin up a call and validate a prototype instantly. We don't guess; we ask.

  • We move at pace, including on strategic work. Strategy isn't a separate, slower track here - we test it by shipping.

Here's what you can expect to be working on as an L6 Lead Product Designer at Street Group

  • Own the design vision and execution for a product domain. Translate strategic direction into the most ambiguous, cross-cutting, or strategically important pieces of design work.

  • Set the craft bar through your own output. The work you ship is the reference point for what good looks like in your area.

  • Own the cross-cutting design problems: patterns across multiple features, flows across multiple surfaces, the coherence of the domain's experience as a whole.

  • Mentor and raise the bar of the designers around you - through critique, pairing, and modelling what excellent design looks like.

  • Drive AI thinking strategically - both in your own workflow (Claude Code, in-product changes, prototype testing) and in what we ship to users. You'll have a strong view on what makes a good AI feature in this domain vs a gimmicky one.

Why you should (and shouldn't) apply

You should apply if:

  • You've operated at senior IC level in a modern product org and you want broader scope to influence what gets built.

  • You're commercially fluent. You've made design trade-offs informed by how the product makes money, not just by user preference. You can name those trade-offs and defend them either way.

  • You define what success looks like before you ship, and you read the result against it after. Metrics, support data, customer feedback - you go and look.

  • You have strong, well-formed views on AI in product design and have put them into practice. You can articulate when AI is the right design solution and when it isn't.

  • You move at pace on strategic work, not just on features.

You probably shouldn't apply if:

  • You're looking for the next pay band up from Senior with broadly similar expectations. This is not a "Senior+" role. Lead expects materially more scope, autonomy, judgment, and ownership of outcomes.

  • You've never shipped design work where you defined a success measure upfront and checked the result afterwards. We need someone who already operates that way.

  • You've never had to make a commercial trade-off - design that's user-optimal but expensive to build, or design that doesn't move retention.

  • You'd struggle to explain how AI is changing what you ship, not just how you work. AI fluency is non-negotiable at this level.

  • You expect to be handed a brief. At L6 you identify what's worth doing and bring the case for it.

A bit about you

  • Experience: Roughly 8+ years of Product/UX Design experience, with a track record at senior IC level. SaaS or complex product experience is strongly preferred.

  • Outcomes, not artefacts: You can point to design work you've shipped where you wrote the success measure upfront and read the result after release. You know what worked, what didn't, and what you'd do differently.

  • Commercial fluency: You understand how the products you've worked on make money and you've made trade-offs informed by that.

  • AI: Comfortable using AI across your workflow and equally comfortable thinking strategically about AI in the products you design - what makes a good AI feature, what the failure modes are, what to build now vs later.

About Genesis

We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco, London and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration and the pursuits they love for their own sake.

We're building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model and we are starting to put it to work with real customers.

The role

General-purpose robots learn from real, dexterous human work, the kind of data that does not exist on the internet. We capture it with our own collection hardware: a person wears it, does the work, and the robot learns to do it too.

You will be a senior member of the team scaling our data collection operation in Paris, working closely with our Paris research and engineering teams and with the operation in the Bay Area.

You will help lead the day-to-day execution and quality bar on the Paris floor while remaining deeply hands-on with data collection, teleoperation, task setup, and real-robot testing. You will wear our gloves and cameras, teleoperate our hardware, and take ownership of complex collection requests from setup through execution and quality review.

You will work shoulder to shoulder with our model engineering and research teams, turning their requests into physical demonstrations and feeding what you learn on the floor back to them. You will be expected to operate autonomously, help guide and train other operators and contribute to how the Paris operation evolves as the team grows.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You will not just run existing tasks: you will help shape how they are executed, how quality is measured, and how other operators are trained to deliver consistently.

What you will do

  • Help lead the Paris data collection floor. Set the execution and quality bar for day-to-day collection work and help the team scale effectively.

  • Own complex collection setups. Take a loosely defined request and turn it into a working, repeatable collection task, including the setup, fixtures, props, environment, and procedure, with minimal support from engineering.

  • Create high-quality training data. Wear our gloves and cameras, teleoperate our hardware, and produce precise demonstrations that can be used to train our models.

  • Own the full collection workflow. Go beyond collecting the data itself: review and quality-check your work, identify unusable episodes, support annotation, and help ensure that what reaches research is trainable data.

  • Build repeatable tasks. Turn new collection requests into clear, repeatable processes that can be executed consistently by other operators.

  • Partner with research and model engineering. Translate their requests into physical collection tasks, share observations from the floor, and iterate with them on setups and collection strategy.

  • Improve the operation. Identify when a fixture, station layout, procedure, or collection method can be improved and proactively help implement those improvements.

  • Write and improve the playbook. Own SOPs, quality checks, and training materials that allow the Paris operation to scale while maintaining a consistent quality bar.

  • Guide other operators. Help onboard, train, and mentor operators and reinforce consistent execution across the team.

  • Run real-robot testing. Partner with reliability and engineering teams to test robots on the floor, document what you observe, and help surface issues.

  • Own quality. Review your own work and the team's, take direct feedback, and keep raising the bar.

What we are looking for

  • You have done precise, repetitive physical work to a high quality bar and can explain what made your work good and how you measured it. This could include data collection, teleoperation, motion capture, robotics lab work, assembly, fine craft, or another hands-on technical environment.

  • Hands-on robot or glove-based data collection experience is a strong plus, but not a requirement. This kind of data collection is new, and we will teach you our specific tools and approach.

  • You build, not just run. Give you a vague request and a scrappy setup, and you can turn it into a clean, repeatable task with the right fixtures, environment, process, and written procedure.

  • You can operate autonomously. You are comfortable taking ownership of complex collection tasks with limited day-to-day support from engineering.

  • You understand quality beyond collection. You can review your work, recognize when collected data is unusable or below the quality bar, and understand why.

  • You are ready to lead. You have trained, mentored, or led others doing hands-on work and want to help establish the execution and quality standard for a growing team.

  • You work well with research and engineering teams. You can translate their requests into physical collection tasks and turn what you observe during collection into useful feedback.

  • You have exceptional attention to detail. You notice the moment something about the setup, hardware, environment, procedure, or collected data is off.

  • You are technically handy. You are comfortable with Linux, some Python scripting to automate repetitive work, and hardware assembly and troubleshooting.

  • You are comfortable in a fast-moving environment. Hardware, processes, and collection methods will evolve quickly, and you are comfortable adapting while helping improve how the team works.

  • You communicate well in English. You will work daily with teams in Paris and the Bay Area across time zones. French is a plus.

  • Bonus: reliability testing. You have partnered with a reliability or test team on real-robot testing.

Working conditions and role constraints

  • Work takes place in production environments and technical laboratories.

  • Prolonged standing and repetitive hand and arm movements while wearing collection equipment, including gloves, head-mounted cameras, and headsets, for extended periods.

  • Handling and lifting of loads, including props, fixtures, robot equipment, and station equipment, up to 23 kg for station setup and reconfiguration.

Why this role

  • Real ownership. You will have meaningful ownership over how the Paris data collection floor operates and help set the standard the team grows toward.

  • Hands-on leadership. You will remain close to the work while helping guide other operators, improve execution, and raise the quality bar.

  • Build, not just execute. You will take ambiguous collection needs and turn them into reliable, repeatable tasks that can scale across the team.

  • A clear growth path. As the operation scales, this role can grow toward leading or supervising teams of operators or toward broader project and program management responsibilities.

  • The front line of the mission. The data you create, review, and improve is what teaches our robots to work.

At machineMD in Bern we’re on a mission to radically improve the measurement of brain function through standardized, automated, quantitative exams. You’ll develop our test automation with support from developers, requirements engineers, and testers.     Functie  Reliability engineer

     

    Beschrijving functie

     

    De reliability engineer is een productie specialist die de totale levensduur van installatie bestudeert en analyseert hoe het bedrijf omgaat met investeringen en onderhoud van assets.  De reliability engineer is de expert in het identificeren van potentiële risico’s en het voorkomen van stilstanden. Daar problemen moeilijk volledig te voorkomen zijn, geeft de reliability engineer adviezen hoe te handelen bij storingen die plaatsvinden. Het doel is te voorkomen dat fouten in productiesystemen optreden.

     

    De reliability engineer analyseert tevens de veiligheidsrisico’s geassocieerd met installatie fouten. Ter voorkoming van stilstand maakt de reliability engineer onderhoudsschema’s en analyseert statistische gegevens die helpen te voorspellen wanneer en hoe fouten voor kunnen komen. De reliability engineer ontwikkelt inspectie criteria die gebruikt worden om de asset health te monitoren. 



    Om dit te kunnen bereiken maakt de reliability engineer gebruik van een aantal technieken.

     

  • Voorlopige gevaren analyse: Preliminary hazard analysis is de initiële identificatie van potentiële gevaren en fouten in een productie proces of systeem

  • Failure modes and effect analysis ( FMEA): Betreft het opsommen van de manieren dat een proces of systeem kan falen en wat de consequenties hiervan zijn.

  • Criticality analysis: bepaalt hoe ernstig de consequenties zijn van een asset fout voor het productiesysteem van het bedrijf.

  • Onderhoudbaarheid: gedetailleerde informatie hoe efficiënt en betrouwbaar het bedrijf een onderdeel kan repareren.

  • Foutenboom analyse: onderzoek van een systeem fout door naar de kleinere voorafgaande gebeurtenissen te kijken die hebben bijgedragen aan de systeem fout

    Are you a security specialist in the OT space looking to expand your expertise into cloud solutions? Are you a cloud security champion passionate about bringing your expertise into OT/IoT space? At Priva Product Development Organisation we are looking for the Security Architect who will shape the security of our products.  

      

    Security Architect in Priva Product Development – Why this role matters 

    At Priva, we develop hardware products and software services for horticulture and building automation. Seeing the importance of our products for our customers, we recognize the need to continuously keep these secure in the ever evolving, fast-paced world. The security requirements in our landscape span four different areas: 

    1. Physical/embedded device security. 

    1. OT (operational technology) network security. 

    1. OT network to Priva-hosted cloud services communications. 

    1. Priva's hybrid on-prem/multi-cloud platform applications security, including applications, infrastructure, CI/CD pipelines.  

    What makes this role truly unique is that our products contain long-lived hardware components that our customers run for years. Engineering future-proofed security solutions and maintaining a security posture at existing sites across all these areas having wide range of varying implementations and security needs creates a great challenge and a great fun. 

    As part of the architecture team, you will play a key role in shaping the future of Priva's portfolio offered on the global market. You define security standards, security practices and security designs for our products that are used in tens of thousands of buildings and greenhouses. You work across product, engineering, and operations teams to ensure security controls and adhered to, implemented and tested as you have designed these. That’s real impact. 

    What you will be doing 

    As a Security Architect, you have a very simple mission: you see to it that Priva's hardware products and software (cloud) services are secured against known and emergent threats in lines with the industry standards and practices. You build upon your strong background in securing device/OT networks, cloud applications, and engraining the security practices in the daily work of Agile teams to achieve consistent security posture across all Priva products, designs, and customer deployments. 

     As a security architect, you are trusted counterpart of Priva Security, Quality, and Compliance officer to define, review, and execute controls arising from ISO9001 and ISO27001 standards and internal initiatives. You are responsible for presenting the necessary evidence of Priva’s compliance with these controls to the auditors. 

    • Security standards, policies, and design patterns library 

    • Security architecture review process 

    • Risk register and residual risk acceptance documentation 

    • Periodic product security implementation reviews, including maintaining non-compliance register 

    • Defined requirements, products and work packages for security-focused projects with 3rd party service providers, reviewing and accepting their deliverables, and supervising the implementation of these deliverables in the Priva hardware products and software services. 

    • Regulatory compliance (IEC 62443-4, ISO 27001, ISO 9001 or other standard that may be applicable in specific geographies) 

    • Threat intelligence briefing relevant to OT/IoT threat landscape 

    • Designing, implementing, and reviewing security controls applied at major customer sites. 

    Above all, this is a hands-on role – occasionally writing code is included. You connect the industry’s best practices, ISO standards, product vision with the daily work of the product team. As a security architect, you practice what you preach. You explain, coach, and show by example the implementation of security as Secure SDLC in the developer’s daily work.  

    To succeed in this role: 

    • You are passionate about OT security; you have great interest in the application of our products in the field. You are curious to grasp how our products truly work for our customers to find the best balance between security, reliability, and cost. You share the opinion that "if I don't secure Priva’s applications, then no one else will". 

    • You identify and eliminate issues in the development cycle that can jeopardize the security posture. You know and can show by example how to "test securely as well as test security" 

    • You are a great collaborator who can be a valuable sparring partner with product managers to understand and refine customer's needs for security so that you define the right security designs for market segments. Engineering managers rely on your ability to steer security implementations within the product teams. 

    • You are comfortable designing products that our customers will be running for years; comfortable providing guidance to LCM activities for existing customers to update hardware and software components to continuously stay secure. 

    • You share the knowledge about security subjects; you explain why security practices exist and what they achieve in the long run. 

    • You can translate security designs into engineering specifications, appraise implementation designs, conduct code reviews. This role with a strong hands-on component, not just a pure governance role. 

    • You understand and can register, document, and communicate clearly risks and trade-offs between differen t project execution scenarios 

    • You have had hands-on experience implementing security designs using modern programming language and frameworks, and you are able to coach product teams to increase their secure coding maturity e.g. by running threat modelling workshops with the engineering team. 

    • You have vast experience with architecture roles with 3-5 years of experience specifically focusing on security. 

    In addition, you have the following technical expertise: 

    • Proven track record across at least two of the three domains: OT/IoT/embedded security, network security, cloud security 

    • You are familiar with modern authentication and authorization frameworks (JWT, OpenID, SAML) and (REST) API security and protection approached 

    • ISO 27001 and IEC 62443-4 understanding at a working level 

    • Working knowledge with or excellent ability to apply the PKI and certificate lifecycle management at scale; also, with the vision how to implement this in OT/IoT deployment contexts 

    • Solid network security understanding: firewall policy, micro-segmentation, DMZ design for IT/OT boundaries 

    • Zero trust architecture principles 

    • Secure SDLC and DevSecOps tools and practices (think about OWASP, SANS25, Snyk, Black Duck, etc) 

      


    The following competence is desired: 

    • OT/ICS protocols and architectures (such as BACnet Secure Connect, Modbus, DNP3, MQTT, AMQP) 

    • Embedded device security for industrial PCs, systems-on-chip, and microcontrollers: secure boot, hardware security modules (HSMs), TPM, secure enclave concepts, firmware & data signing, encryption 

    • Cloud security on at least one major platform (AWS, Azure, or GCP) 

    • Container and Kubernetes security 

    • Secrets management and key management systems (HashiCorp Vault, AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) 

    • Priva's technical stack is C#/C++/.NET and Angular. Experience implementing production projects with this stack is preferred, but not required if you are able to learn it quickly (based on your vast experience) 

    What we offer you 

      

    💶 Excellent remuneration — competitive and aligned with experience. 

    🌴 30 days holiday per year, with the option to buy 5 more at half price. 

    🏦 Excellent pension contribution. 

    🎓 Education budget of €1,000 per year. 

    ⏰ Flexible working hours. 

    🍱 Onsite canteen (e.g., poke bowl for €2). 

    🏋️ Free onsite gym. 

    🎉 Vibrant, open culture.

    About the role

    As the Senior Product Manager on our AI team, you'll own how AI shows up in Tebi, from an AI agent embedded in the product to the AI capabilities that run through the platform. Tebi sits on a unified foundation of sales, payments, reservations, kitchen and inventory data, which gives our AI something most restaurant software can't offer: the full picture.     What you’ll do:

    • Define how we measure quality and trust in AI features, including evals, accuracy, adoption and merchant outcomes, and use that to iterate quickly.

    • Decide where AI belongs in the product and where it doesn't, including guardrails, human-in-the-loop moments and when the merchant makes the final call.

    We use AI the way our merchants use Tebi, to cut out the friction and get to what matters faster. We believe in a world where AI increases quality, efficiency and speed.

    At Tebi, AI isn't a policy or a checkbox, it's just part of how we work. It helps us write, analyse, build, and improve but doesn't make the last call. If there's a smarter way to do something, we want to find it.

The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

Hybrid in Berlin or London

We’re looking for a Growth Product Manager

Own the systems that decide which German businesses iwoca reaches, and the journey they take from first click to submitted loan application. You’ll join a team that is still being built, with a data scientist in place and engineers being hired in parallel. A good fit if you like working from first principles, and would rather run an experiment than win an argument.

The team

The DE Acquisition Tech team builds the systems behind how German businesses discover iwoca and apply for funding: the models that decide which businesses to approach, the eligibility checks that tell a business early whether iwoca can help, and the signup flow itself. Product, analytics, data science and engineering sit in the same squad by design, so the team can go from hypothesis to shipped change without waiting on anyone else. The German marketing and sales teams depend on this work: the team’s models decide who they contact, and its journeys decide how many of those businesses convert.

The team is being built right now. It currently includes a data scientist, and we’re hiring engineers in parallel – so you would join early enough to shape how the team operates.

The role

This role sits between iwoca’s German commercial teams – marketing, sales and commercial strategy – and the technical squad that builds for them. Reporting into the Head of Direct Acquisition, you will own acquisition and activation outcomes for the German market: finding the opportunities, defining the hypotheses, and working with engineering, data, marketing and sales to build, test and iterate.

The scope is broad. We’re not looking for someone with deep expertise in every domain the team covers – spanning product development, analytics, UX and data science – but rather someone intellectually curious, and skilled at asking the right questions.

Own the funnel from first visit to application

  • Own every step of that journey, including the signup flow itself and the eligibility checks inside it.

  • Set the roadmap for acquisition and the signup journey, and decide what the squad builds next.

  • Own the scoring and segmentation that decides where marketing spends and who sales calls first.

Build with your technical squad

  • Ship lead scoring systems, eligibility checkers and signup flows with the team’s data scientist and the engineers we’re hiring.

  • Rework website content, signup flows and decisioning logic with marketing and sales, to convert more of the businesses that already reach iwoca.

  • Strip friction out of the signup journey, so that applying for funding takes minutes rather than an afternoon.

Be the first call when the numbers look wrong

  • Act as the technical partner for German marketing, sales and channel management on attribution, tracking and data pipeline problems.

  • Investigate and resolve data quality issues – broken dashboards, misattributed traffic, unexplained volume changes – often at short notice.

  • Give channel managers access to, and guidance on, the attribution logic behind their numbers.

  • Keep the tracking and attribution systems trustworthy, so every decision downstream rests on numbers the team believes.

Run the experiments that decide what ships

  • Design, run and interpret A/B tests across messaging, targeting, eligibility checks and signup flows.

  • Find opportunities from first principles, backed by data, customer research and funnel analysis.

Shape how a new team works

  • Direct the squad’s work day to day: brief the data scientist and engineers, set priorities, and turn their models into shipped products.

  • Define the priorities, roles and rituals of a team that is still being built.

  • Lead cross-functional initiatives with marketing and sales, aligning them with engineering and data on shared goals, hypotheses and success metrics.

  • Turn the commercial strategy team’s goals into testable hypotheses and briefs the squad can act on.

The requirements

Essential:

  • Experience as a product manager, growth product manager, or in a role with clear ownership of product-led growth outcomes.

  • Strong analytical capability and experience with experimentation frameworks and A/B testing tools.

  • Hands-on experience with tracking and attribution setups, such as Amplitude, GA4, GTM, server-side tagging or conversion feedback into ad platforms.

  • Able to act as the product voice on modelling work – challenging assumptions and turning model output into decisions, without building the models yourself.

  • Strong capability using AI tools, including structured prompting and iterative AI interaction to problem solve and increase productivity.

Bonus:

  • Experience in fintech, lending, B2B SaaS, or regulated products.

  • Experience working with data science teams or involvement in modelling projects.

  • Fluency in German and strong written communication skills tailored to customer-facing environments.

  • Knowledge of the German SME ecosystem or B2B financial products.

  • Experience working in or helping build newly formed teams.

The salary

We expect to pay from £60,000 - £80,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture

At iwoca, we prioritise a culture of learning, growth, and support, and invest in the development of our team members. We value thought and skill diversity, and encourage people to explore new areas of interest, adopt better tools – including AI – and apply sound judgement so our products and decisions improve over time.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

  • Flexible working hours.

  • Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

  • A choice between a dedicated dental plan or a health cash plan that reimburses everyday medical expenses.

  • A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

  • 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

  • A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

  • Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

  • 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

  • An employee equity incentive scheme.

  • Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

  • Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

  • Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

  • A learning and development budget for everyone.

  • Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

  • Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

About us

Salience Labs is developing optical circuit switching technology for AI infrastructure, aimed at significantly reducing latency and cost in data centre networks. As we move towards real-world deployment, you’ll have genuine ownership of your area, working alongside a highly technical team of physicists, engineers and software specialists on one of the hardest problems in AI infrastructure.

Job Overview

As an Embedded Software Engineer at Salience Labs, you’ll be right at the centre of our photonics product development. This role spans low-level firmware, rapid prototyping, and systems integration, giving you the chance to influence everything from proof-of-concept devices to our commercial platforms. You’ll collaborate across hardware, photonics, and FPGA teams to ensure smooth, efficient embedded software development, right down to the register level and all the way up to application-facing tools.

This is a full-stack embedded role, where versatility and curiosity are just as important as technical depth. We’re looking for engineers who enjoy working close to the metal, but can just as easily contribute to user-facing tools and test infrastructure. You’ll be part of a small, fast-paced team where autonomy is encouraged and impact is tangible.

What you’ll be doing

  • Design, implement, and document embedded software across a variety of project scales

  • Work closely with hardware and FPGA teams to build robust embedded systems

  • Use off-the-shelf development kits for rapid prototyping and system testing

  • Select, tailor, and integrate open-source applications and embedded frameworks

  • Collaborate with the Systems Test team to support test automation and data capture

  • Develop internal tools and test benches for the photonics and hardware teams

What we’re looking for

  • 4+ years of hands-on experience developing embedded software in C or C++

  • Proven ability to own software modules from design to delivery

  • Comfortable using Python and modern tooling (Git, Confluence, Jira)

  • Strong problem-solver with clear analytical thinking and communication skills

  • Flexible team player, able to switch between solo work and close collaboration

Even better if you

  • Can read schematics or interpret RTL, particularly helpful for supporting hardware teams

  • Have experience developing for ARM-based embedded platforms

  • Know your way around I2C, SPI, PCIe, and embedded driver development

  • Understand networking concepts

  • Are comfortable becoming a domain expert in unfamiliar tools or technologies

This is a high-impact role for someone who thrives on building, testing, and iterating in real hardware environments. If you’re looking for a deeply technical role where you can have influence across the full product stack, and you like the sound of building the software brains of next-gen optical systems, then we’d love to hear from you.

    About us

    Owkin is an agentic AI company pioneering Biological Artificial Superintelligence to solve problems in biology where human researchers alone have failed.
    Owkin builds K Pro - an AI scientist for pharmaceutical research and strategic decision-making. K Pro orchestrates a suite of AI skills and tools to decode complex biology, accelerate research, and dramatically increase productivity.

    About the role:

     We are seeking a driven Research Scientist with hands-on expertise in Foundation Models (FMs) and Multimodal AI to help drive the next phase of our machine learning platform.

    In this role, you will bridge cutting-edge AI research and practical application. Rather than training massive base models from scratch, your focus will be on fine-tuning, adapting, and aligning open-weights foundation models across diverse data modalities (e.g. structured tabular data, single-cell scRNA-seq, image representations, and natural language) to build multimodal systems.

     

    In particular, you will be responsible for:

    • Model adaptation and optimization: Adapt, fine-tune, and evaluate state-of-the-art open-source foundation models (e.g., domain-specific transformers, vision-language models) using fine-tuning and transfer learning strategies.

    • Multimodal integration: Design and implement cross-modal alignment architectures (e.g., contrastive learning, projection heads, unified embedding spaces) to fuse structured, sequential, and text/image data layers.

    • Pipeline and evaluation engineering: Build rigorous, domain-tailored benchmarking frameworks and evaluation pipelines to validate model reliability, generalization, and downstream task performance.

    • Applied R&D collaboration: Work closely with cross-functional teams (data engineers, domain specialists, and software engineers) to integrate adapted models into scalable production and inference workflows.

    • Low-hanging fruit innovation: Identify high-impact, incremental improvements in data pre-processing, embedding representation, and fine-tuning to maximize model performance without unnecessary computational overhead.

    Required qualifications / experience:

    • Education: Ph.D. or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Mathematics or a related quantitative field.

    • Experience: 2-4 years of post-degree experience applying deep learning and foundation models to complex datasets.

    • Foundation models: Demonstrated experience adapting and fine-tuning foundation models.

    • Multimodal learning: Proven experience with cross-modal representation learning, joint embedding alignment (e.g., CLIP-style architectures), or vision-language models.

    • Technical stack:

      • Advanced proficiency in Python and modern deep learning frameworks (PyTorch, Hugging Face ecosystem).

      • Hands-on experience with fine-tuning techniques.

      • Familiarity with data engineering tools for handling large-scale or multi-modal datasets (Parquet, AnnData, HDF5).

     Preferred qualifications/bonus:

    • Experience working with biological or omics data (e.g., scRNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, clinical and/or histology data).

    • Experience deploying or scaling models using containerized environments (Docker, Kubernetes) and cloud infrastructure (AWS/GCP).

    • Track record of open-source contributions or peer-reviewed publications at top ML conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR) or domain-specific journals.

    About Us

    Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

    Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

    About the Role

    As SAR Remote Sensing Engineer, you are the subject matter expert on applying advanced signal processing and machine learning to SAR data within our RF analytics team. You own the analytics layer end to end: algorithm design, real-time implementation and field validation on real captures from our own platforms. You will also shape the move toward multi-modal solutions that combine SAR with optical and RF sensor feeds. Cycles are measured in months, and the scope grows with the company.

    Responsibilities

    • Lead initiatives using SAR polarimetry and coherence for automated change detection.

    • Design and prototype state-of-the-art machine learning models for SAR image segmentation.

    • Develop algorithms for target detection and object classification on SAR data.

    • Fuse SAR with optical, RF and other data sources to support GNSS-denied operations.

    • Port algorithms from Python prototypes to real-time pipelines with software and embedded/FPGA teams.

    • Build the capture, labelling and replay tooling that makes performance claims reproducible.

    • Validate performance on simulated and real-world datasets, in the lab and on field-test campaigns.

    • Work with radar, radio, electronic warfare and computer vision teams to define what the analytics layer needs from each sensor.

    Candidate Requirements

    • Master’s or PhD in electrical engineering, telecommunications engineering, signal processing, applied mathematics or a related field.

    • 3+ years of experience in radar signal processing or SAR remote sensing.

    • Deep understanding of SAR phenomenology and its information content, including coherence, amplitude, phase and polarimetry.

    • Theoretical and practical expertise in machine learning, both deep learning and classical techniques.

    • Experience taking at least one algorithm from prototype to real hardware running on real signals.

    • Strong Python skills and sound engineering practices (Git, code reviews, testing, documentation).

    • Exposure to GEOINT, ELINT or SIGINT work is a plus, and you are comfortable with defense security vetting.

    The question

    Generating one image with a diffusion model means evaluating a large neural network tens to hundreds of times. That repetition is where the energy goes, and it is part of why data-centre demand is now visible at grid scale: the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory puts US data-centre electricity use at 176 TWh in 2023, 4.4 % of national consumption, a figure that more than doubled since 2017 largely because of AI servers, and projects 325–580 TWh by 2028. Emerging hardware attacks exactly this primitive: analog in-memory computing, silicon photonics, ferroelectric devices and stochastic computing perform the underlying matrix–vector products at lower energy than digital CMOS, under conditions on scale and precision, but return a perturbed result. The usual objection is that nobody can say in advance how much perturbation a model tolerates. In EMMA, this opportunity is pursued through a PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine as the primary demonstrator, complemented where appropriate by FeFET-based analog computing, so that device-level non-idealities are treated as explicit design parameters rather than as after-the-fact implementation losses. Diffusion models are an unusual case in which that question has a mathematical answer: their convergence theory bounds the discrepancy between the generated and target distributions by three terms, of which only one, the L 2 error of the learned score, depends on the hardware. That side is now in good shape: for stochastic samplers, bounds linear in the dimension under minimal assumptions on the data; for deterministic samplers, a matching theory under regularity. What is missing is the bridge. The theory is parameterised by a score error, the hardware literature by conductance noise, effective number of bits and photons per multiply–accumulate; nobody has written the map between them, in either direction. The quantisation literature for diffusion models reports image-quality scores; the induced L 2 score error, in the form the convergence theory needs, is directly measurable and goes unreported. One open sub-question sets the direction: the distinction between an error redrawn at each evaluation, as in stochastic computing, and an error frozen at write time, as in deterministic quantisation, has been settled in one setting only, and not the one hardware lives in; carrying it over is what this position exists to do. The work is judged on one concrete outcome. For at least one architecture, we want to show that theenergy gain from moving the score evaluation off digital CMOS is real, measured where it survives integration and not extrapolated from a single tile, and that it is paid for by a loss in sample quality that is small and, above all, tunable: a knob the designer sets, whose position the theory predicts rather than discovers afterwards.

    What you will do

    The work is organised in four packages, summarised below; the full research programme is available from the supervisors on request.

    1. Make the score error measurable, starting from Gaussian targets where the whole error decomposition is closed-form. You will report the induced score error for a given perturbation of the network’s arithmetic, the number the theory needs and the quantisation literature does not report.

    2. Map device physics onto the theory. Propagate the published error models for the technologies INL works on through the score network into an explicit score-error budget, separating what is proved from what is measured.

    3. Extend the guarantees. Existing bounds assume a deterministic oracle, or a benign randomised one; extend them to error that is part frozen at write time and part redrawn at each call, and settle, on the way, which process the score error should be controlled along.

    4. Co-design with INL, and deliver the proof of concept. Turn the score-error budget into an energy– accuracy frontier for INL’s PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine, using device-calibrated circuitlevel models; a FeFET-based analog alternative may be considered where appropriate. Jointly vary sampler steps, stochastic bitstream length and effective precision to identify an operating point predicted to yield a real energy advantage over digital CMOS at a small, tunable loss in sample quality. The result is a frontier predicted from mathematical and hardware models, then verified against calibrated measurements.

    A clear negative answer is more useful to us than a vague positive one: a negative result on point 3 leaves points 1 and 2 intact and turns point 4 from a prediction into a measurement.

    • A PhD in applied mathematics, statistics, machine learning, electronic engineering, computer science or a closely related field, obtained (or with the defence scheduled) before the start of the contract.

    • A strong foundation in probability and stochastic analysis, numerical analysis, optimisation, or machine learning: SDEs, Girsanov’s theorem, time reversal of diffusions, with the ability to apply it rigorously to diffusion or other generative models.

    • Familiarity with the convergence theory of sampling algorithms, or the demonstrated capacity to acquire it quickly, for example through Langevin/MCMC analysis, optimal transport or concentration of measure.

    • Solid scientific computing (PyTorch or JAX), and the habit of writing code others can run. Ability and motivation to work across mathematical modelling and hardware-aware AI.

    • Working English; French is not required.

    Valued, not required

    Prior work on diffusion or score-based generative models; numerical analysis of finite-precision arithmetic. Familiarity with hardware-aware machine learning, approximate or stochastic computing, analogue in-memory computing, device modelling, circuit simulation, photonics, ferroelectric devices, or energy modelling. Experience linking model accuracy or robustness to implementation non-idealities, such as quantisation, noise, drift, variability, finite precision, or correlated errors. Evidence of interdisciplinary research, for example work at the interface of mathematics, machine learning, devices, circuits, architectures, or electronic-design automation. No hardware experience is expected or needed to apply.

    What matters most

    We are seeking a researcher who wants to explore how to turn physical constraints into mathematical and architectural design parameters. The project does not require prior laboratory hardware experience: INL provides device expertise, measured characteristics and modelling infrastructure. However, the successful candidate must be prepared to engage critically with non-ideal analog, photonic and ferroelectric accelerators, and to work with both supervisors to connect device-level error mechanisms, score-error guarantees and the energy–quality trade-off of diffusion-model inference.     About the role

    As Data Platform Manager you will own Destinus's company data platform. Built on Microsoft Fabric, it brings together data from our different systems, and it serves the reporting and data agents that production, supply chain, program management, and finance work from every week.

    You will own its architecture: how OneLake and our lakehouses are structured, how data lands in them from the systems we run, and how it holds up as more of the business comes to depend on it. You will lead a small team of data engineers — setting direction, reviewing their work, growing them — and you will keep building yourself. You are also the person who makes our AI ambitions possible: the foundation behind our data agents and our Company Brain is yours to design and deliver.

    At Destinus we are redefining the future of aerospace manufacturing, building advanced Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) across three European plants. The data you will work with is physical — parts, build progress, shortages, non-conformances — and the questions asked of it get harder each year as we grow. If you want a platform you can still shape rather than one already set in concrete, this is a good moment to arrive.

    What You'll Do

    • Own the architecture of our Microsoft Fabric estate end to end — OneLake, our lakehouses and their bronze, silver, and gold layers, workspace and domain structure, naming conventions, and the standards that keep it coherent as it grows.
    • Lead, mentor, and grow a small team of data engineers: set priorities, review code, raise the technical bar, and develop the people.
    • Stay hands-on. You will build pipelines, notebooks, and Delta tables yourself, not only direct others who do.
    • Own the integrations that land data in OneLake from our source systems — ERP, HR, shopfloor, quality, and the business applications that come after them — choosing sensibly between Data Factory pipelines, dataflows, shortcuts, and mirroring for each source.
    • Own the gold layer and the semantic models built on it, so that Power BI reads from one governed source rather than from copies scattered around the business.
    • Work closely with our Business Operations & Data Specialists, who represent the business owners of each domain: turn their requirements into the right gold tables, agree definitions with them, and give them a platform they can query, validate, and explain to the business with confidence.
    • Own lineage across the estate: know what feeds what, be able to prove it to an auditor, and make dependencies visible rather than tribal knowledge.
    • Build the data foundation for our AI programme — the lakehouse structures, pipelines, and knowledge graph behind our Fabric data agents and our Company Brain — and deliver it to a standard that can be trusted with a real question.
    • Design and maintain the OneLake security and access model together with your team: workspace roles, access groups, and the controls that decide who sees what in the lake.
    • Keep the platform reliable, observable, and cost-aware: monitoring, alerting, recovery, and disciplined use of our Fabric capacity — including knowing what a runaway notebook costs us.

    Requirements

    What You’ll Need

    Requirements

    • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Engineering, or a related field.
    • 5-8 years of data engineering experience, including real ownership of a lakehouse architecture rather than only delivering against someone else's.
    • Hands-on Microsoft Fabric experience is strongly preferred — OneLake, lakehouses, Delta tables, the SQL analytics endpoint, Data Factory pipelines, Spark notebooks, and semantic models in Direct Lake mode. If your depth is in Azure Synapse, Databricks, or Data Lake Storage Gen2 and you have since moved onto Fabric in earnest, we will take that seriously.
    • Strong command of the medallion pattern and of Delta Lake in practice: partitioning, schema evolution, table maintenance, and why a gold table behaves the way it does.
    • Genuinely hands-on. Strong SQL, solid PySpark, and comfort building and orchestrating pipelines yourself. This is not a role that stops at diagrams.
    • Practical understanding of Fabric capacity: how workloads consume it, how to spot what is burning it, and how to keep the platform inside its envelope.
    • Experience leading engineers — formally, or as a technical lead who set direction and mentored others. A first step into people management is welcome if the technical leadership is already there.
    • Proven integration experience with ERP systems such as Microsoft Dynamics 365 / MSD, as well as APIs, flat-file landings, and change data capture from operational databases.
    • Solid data modelling skills, including dimensional modelling and an understanding of how a semantic layer serves Power BI.
    • Working knowledge of lineage, data governance, and access control in a cloud platform; exposure to Microsoft Purview is a plus.
    • Interest or experience in the data foundations behind AI assistants — retrieval, knowledge graphs, and preparing data so that an agent can answer with it.
    • Aerospace or another regulated industry is an advantage; so is experience in a start-up or scale-up.
    • Fluent in English; additional European languages are a plus.

    Who You Are

    You are an architect who never stops building. You have strong opinions about how a platform should be structured, and you earn the right to them by being in the code. You would rather make a design decision explicit and documented than let it live in one person's head.

    You care more about reliability than novelty. You know that the measure of a data platform is whether people trust the numbers that come out of it on a Monday morning, not how modern the stack looks on a slide. When something breaks, you want to know why it was possible, not just how to patch it.

    You enjoy growing engineers, and you understand that leading a small team means doing the work alongside them. Above all, you want to build something durable — a foundation that holds while the company scales on top of it.

    • Able to explain data to finance colleagues and accounting logic to technical ones — and to get both sides to agree on one definition.

We run on D365, and someone who already knows it will be effective months earlier. An interest in improving how the system is configured and used matters as much as knowing where to click.
    • A track record of simplifying or automating a process, not only reporting on it.
    • Experience supporting an external audit, or working in a multi-entity, multi-currency international group, is a strong advantage.
    • Fluent in English; additional European languages are a plus.
    • Experience in a start-up or scale-up environment is preferred.

    Who You Are

    You are precise, and you are curious about where a number came from before you are comfortable reporting it — whether that means reading the ledger or querying the lakehouse. You know the difference between a figure that looks right and a figure that can be traced back to its source, and you care about the second one.

    • Improve the finance processes and system configuration that create the data, working with the finance team and our ERP specialists, so that issues are fixed at source rather than corrected every month.
    • Help the finance team get more from the tools through training and self-service, so they can answer their own questions.

    • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Finance, Accounting, Controlling, Economics, or a related field.

We run on D365, and someone who already knows it will be effective months earlier. An interest in improving how the system is configured and used matters as much as knowing where to click.
    • A track record of simplifying or automating a process, not only reporting on it.

    • Fluent in English; additional European languages are a plus.
    • Experience in a start-up or scale-up environment is preferred.

    Who You Are

    You are precise, and you are curious about where a number came from before you are comfortable reporting it — whether that means reading the ledger or querying the lakehouse. You know the difference between a figure that looks right and a figure that can be traced back to its source, and you care about the second one.

    You are not content to rebuild the same report every month. When something is manual, repetitive, or fragile, your instinct is to go upstream and fix it rather than absorb it. You enjoy working with finance colleagues who ask hard questions, and you would rather be challenged on a detail than have it slip through.

    Above all, you want your work to be relied on, by the CFO, by the board, and by anyone who audits it.

    • Develop automated analyses on top of the model, such as heat-load, signal-integrity and noise budgets, channel counts, scalability, and full-system metrics such as power consumption as qubit counts grow.

    • Establish requirements traceability from customer and system-level requirements down to component specifications and verification tests.

    • Connect the system model to simulation and measurement data, creating a digital thread between design and test.

    • Drive adoption across the company, training and supporting engineers in using the models and tools in their day-to-day work.

    • Experience with cryogenic, RF/microwave or precision instrumentation systems, or direct experience with superconducting quantum hardware.

    • Background in high-tech, semiconductor, aerospace or scientific instrumentation industries.

    • Experience introducing MBSE into an organisation and driving its adoption.

    • Address performance, latency and scalability of the integrated pipeline, together with algorithm and backend developers.

    • Work hands-on with integrated software and hardware systems at our headquarters and production facility, with occasional on-site visits.

    • Review the work of junior engineers and external development partners in depth, promote good practices for packaging, versioning and release, and share integration knowledge across the team.

    • Competitive salary and benefits package.

    • Enjoy regular team activities and company events.

    • Good communication skills in English and the ability to coordinate with internal teams and external partners.

  • Redis

  • Docker

Front-End

  • StimulusJS or JavaScript ES6

  • Tailwind CSS

  • HTML

  • HTTP

AI Integration

  • Experience integrating AI/ML models (e.g., LLMs, NLP) with web applications

Nice-to-Have Technical Skills

  • Kubernetes for microservices orchestration

  • React for advanced front-end components

  • Graph databases for complex financial data

  • Contributions to open-source RoR or AI projects

Required Soft Skills

  • Entrepreneurial mindset with a passion for AI and FinTech

Why Join Us?

What we’re looking for

  • 3+ years of experience as a full-stack or frontend-heavy engineer.

  • Hands-on experience with AWS for production workloads.

  • Solid understanding of web security best practices (OWASP, secure storage, encryption in transit/at rest, secrets management).

Take-home assignment (Step 1 of the process)

Please complete a take-home assignment. You are allowed to use LLMs to write code. To ensure that your work will not be used at Fluence, we’ve made it unrelated to healthcare:

Build “LendLoop”: a neighborhood tool-lending board with automated workflows

A simple app where neighbors list tools they are willing to lend, request to borrow from each other, and receive automated notifications and reminders handled by n8n.

  • Next.js (App Router)

Public page

  • Show:

Authenticated experience

Job Description Summary

Sandoz is going through an exciting and transformative period as a global leader and pioneering provider of sustainable Biosimilar and Generic medicines. By creating a new and ambitious path, it will provide a unique opportunity for us all, both professionally and personally.

As the Global Marketing Automation Manager at Sandoz, you will lead the design, implementation, and optimization of marketing automation strategies and systems to enhance our digital marketing campaigns. You will be responsible for orchestrating personalized and data-driven marketing efforts to engage healthcare professionals, patients, and stakeholders on a global scale.

Job Description

Key responsibilities:

  • Marketing Automation Strategy:
    • Develop and execute a global marketing automation strategy aligned with the company's marketing objectives, ensuring efficient lead generation, nurturing, and conversion processes
  • Campaign Development and deployment
    • Collaborate with a Team of Global Digital Marketing Managers to design and execute automated customer journeys, ensuring relevance and effectiveness
    • Identify all touchpoints on identification and implementation new customer journey and provide clear interaction plans for multiple markets
  • Automation Platform Management
    • Oversee the implementation, and management of marketing automation platforms such as Scout (SFDC) and Salesforce Marketing Cloud
    • Strong hands-on experience with Salesforce Marketing Cloud (SFMC) is required, including Journey Builder, Audience Builder and Email Studio.
    • Work with MCM channel operations team to ensure effective and efficient use of global digital platforms including latest best practices, updates or releases including new functionalities and channels
  • Performance Analytics
    • Monitor and analyze marketing automation performance, providing insights and recommendations for optimization to enhance campaign effectiveness
  • Compliance and Data Privacy:
    • Ensure marketing automation activities adhere to pharmaceutical industry regulations, including data privacy (e.g., GDPR), and work closely with legal and regulatory teams.
  • Training and Support:
    • Provide training and support to marketing teams and stakeholders in using marketing automation tools effectively.

Our requirements:

  • Proven 3-5 years of experience in Marketing Automation area, (nice to have would be to have an experience within the pharmaceutical or healthcare industry)
  • Strong proficiency in Salesforce Marketing Cloud (SFMC) is required; experience with Salesforce/CRM and other marketing automation tools is an advantage.
  • Strong digital background and successful track of digital initiatives with demonstrated business impact measured by organizational metrics.
  • Strong data analytics and reporting skills.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills.
  • Detail-oriented with a focus on delivering personalized and data-driven marketing experiences.
  • Fluent English.
  • University degree (preferably in Marketing/Business/Economics or related).

Compensation Structure & Criteria:

Sandoz compensation is determined by job level, qualifications, niche skills, experience, and location within company salary ranges. Fully proficient and highly effective employees can expect a starting salary around market median, with those new to the level or with less functional depth at the lower end of the range and those with sustained superior or niche skills towards the higher end of the range. Internal equity and external market data inform our range placement. Annual salary reviews consider performance outcomes, market alignment, and business needs.


Job location: Warsaw, Poland (office)

Work mode: remote

Pay range (monthly salary): gross/zł 15 225- 28 275

Variable compensation:

-annual performance-based bonus: 15%

-employee share program;


Additional benefits include:

• Lunch card worth 450 zł per month

• Laptop,

• Medical care

• Life Insurance

• Retirement plan

• Multisport or Kultura + card (co-financed by the employee)

• Additional 2 days off

• Language learning platform

Pay frequency: monthly

Expected weekly working hours: 40h

Contract type: Replacement employment contract


Why Sandoz?

Generic and Biosimilar medicines are the backbone of the global medicines industry. Sandoz, a leader in this sector, provided more than 900 million patient treatments across 100+ countries in 2024 and while we are proud of this achievement, we have an ambition to do more!

With investments in new development capabilities, production sites, new acquisitions, and partnerships, we have the opportunity to shape the future of Sandoz and help more patients gain access to low-cost, high-quality medicines, sustainably.

Our momentum is powered by an open, collaborative culture driven by our talented and ambitious colleagues, who, in return for applying their skills experience an agile and collegiate environment with impactful, flexible-hybrid careers, where diversity is welcomed and where personal growth is supported!

Join us!

This is a remote role that will be hired in the Eastern Time Zone in the United States.

This position serves as a strategic partner across Credit, Reporting, Data, Product, and Technology organizations, ensuring business, data, process, and system changes are effectively assessed for impacts to Credit Reporting and downstream reporting deliverables.

This role is responsible for performing complex business and data impact assessments, translating business requirements into actionable data use cases, leading data triage, and root cause analysis efforts, and driving improvements in data quality, data lineage transparency, and reporting readiness. The analyst will play a critical role in proactively identifying and mitigating reporting and data risks.

The successful candidate will possess strong credit domain expertise, advanced analytical skills, and the ability to influence senior stakeholders across multiple organizations while independently leading strategic initiatives.


Responsibilities & Qualifications

Duties & Responsibilities:

Credit Reporting Impact Assessment

  • Perform portfolio-level impact assessments to identify reporting, data, and operational risks before implementation.
  • Partner with business stakeholders to ensure reporting requirements are understood and incorporated into change initiatives.

Business & Data Requirements Management

  • Translate business requirements into credit data use cases and actionable requirements for Product, Technology, and Data teams.
  • Develop business process maps, data flow documentation, and reporting requirements to support strategic initiatives.
  • Act as a liaison between business users and technical teams to ensure alignment and successful delivery.

Data Analysis & Data Assurance

  • Perform advanced analysis of credit and reporting data to identify trends, anomalies, risks, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Improve transparency into data quality, data lineage, controls, and reporting readiness across the Credit Reporting ecosystem.
  • Support the design and implementation of processes that enhance data reliability and consumption confidence.

Data Triage & Issue Management

  • Lead data triage activities, root cause analysis, and issue prioritization across multiple stakeholder groups.
  • Coordinate the resolution of data quality, reporting, and operational issues by partnering with business, technology, and data teams.
  • Escalate and communicate material risks and issues to senior stakeholders as appropriate.

Reporting Risk Management

  • Proactively identify, assess, and mitigate reporting and data risks before they impact downstream consumers or regulatory deliverables.
  • Evaluate control effectiveness and recommend enhancements that strengthen reporting accuracy, completeness, and timeliness.
  • Support governance and risk management activities related to Credit Reporting and data management.

Strategic Leadership & Stakeholder Management

  • Independently lead cross-functional initiatives involving Credit, Reporting, Technology, Product, and Data organizations.
  • Influence decision-making by translating complex credit concepts into measurable business and data impacts.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor to senior stakeholders on Credit Reporting, data risk, and reporting readiness matters.

Position Specific Skills:

  • Commercial Banking or Lending Operations Experience
  • Data Quality Management & Data Lineage
  • Cross-Functional Partnership & Collaboration
  • Data Analysis
  • Analytical Thinking
  • Risk Identification & Mitigation

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree and 4 years' experience OR High School Diploma or GED/Equivalent and 8 years' experience in Analytics, or Modeling, or Reporting

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience assessing the impact of data, process, system, or business changes on reporting and regulatory deliverables.
  • Strong understanding of commercial lending, credit products, and the end-to-end credit lifecycle.
  • Experience with data lineage, data governance, data quality, and controls frameworks.
  • Advanced SQL skills and experience analyzing large, complex datasets.
  • Experience performing root cause analysis and leading issue remediation efforts.
  • Knowledge of regulatory reporting, reporting controls, or enterprise risk management practices.
  • Experience working across Credit, Technology, Data, and Reporting organizations.
  • Ability to influence senior leaders and drive outcomes across multiple stakeholder groups.
  • Experience supporting large-scale data transformation, modernization, or credit data initiatives.

Additional Information

As the world’s leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Peraton operates at the critical nexus between traditional and nontraditional threats across all domains: land, sea, space, air, and cyberspace. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees do the can’t be done by solving the most daunting challenges facing our customers. Visit peraton.com to learn how we’re keeping people around the world safe and secure.

Responsibilities

Peraton is seeking an experienced Security Administrator with a primary focus on security administration, audit support, policy management, and third-party risk oversight to maintain a continuous compliance posture against NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, HIPAA, and related frameworks.

The ideal candidate will be a self-starter with strong project management skills, audit experience, and the ability to manage multiple security and compliance workstreams while supporting security leadership, privacy stakeholders, vendors, on-site security engineering teams, and independent assessment organizations.

This selected individual will support our SafeGuard Services (SGS) team, a subsidiary of Peraton, which performs data analysis, investigation, and medical review, to detect, prevent, deter, reduce, and make referrals to recover fraud, waste, and abuse in Medicare/Medicaid healthcare programs.

What you'll do:

The Security Administrator will be responsible for the following but not limited to::

Security Compliance & Policy Management

  • Author, maintain, and update security policies, procedures, standards, plans, and control documentation for the SGS Contracts environment.
  • Perform control testing and gap analysis against NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, HIPAA/HITECH and the CMS ARS and PIM.
  • Document deficiencies and manage the Plan of Action & Milestones (POA&M) lifecycle from identification through verified closure
  • Respond to Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEVs), CCIC bulletins, and compliance data calls

Audit & Assessment Support

  • Support maintenance of the control evidence library and GRC platform records, control mappings, and compliance reporting using CFACTs.
  • Serve as the operational-side evidence provider for annual independent assessments and CMS reviews.
  • Support Security Assessment preparation and security assessment report development
  • Ensure audit-readiness on any given day rather than reconstructed compliance

Third-Party & Vendor Risk Management

  • Conduct vendor security due diligence and assessments.
  • Perform contract and control reviews, continuous monitoring, and risk reporting
  • Manage vendor security questionnaires and ongoing compliance verification

Security Management & Monitoring (SMM) Administration

  • Administer SMM platform documentation, audit activities, and training programs
  • Serve as application owner liaison or support PMO coordination for SMM-related activities
  • Support application ID administration and controls

Physical Security & Access Control

  • Generate and audit Lenel access control reports on a weekly and monthly basis
  • Conduct group audits and access reviews.
  • Support training and onboarding activities

Program & Administrative Support

  • Leverage SharePoint and PowerApps knowledge to streamline workflows and reporting
  • Participate and support change control boards; evaluate applications; participate in technical solutioning and evaluation
  • Support program operations which may include and is not limited to; leading small projects and initiatives, supporting business capture and growth, and providing cross functional support
  • Telework available from EST, MST or CST.time zones.

Qualifications

Basic qualifications:

  • 2 years with BS/BA or 6 years with a HS diploma/equivalent
  • Security Administration experience and the ability to work flexible hours.
  • Experience in security governance, risk, and compliance (GRC), third-party risk management, audit support, and data protection.
  • Experience performing control assessment and gap analysis against NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, and managing the POA&M lifecycle
  • Vendor and Application security risk management experience.
  • Authoring ability for policies, control narratives, and deficiency documentation that withstands external review.
  • Strong analytical and problem‑solving skills, with excellent communication and stakeholder collaboration abilities.
  • US. citizenship required.

Desired qualifications:

  • State & Federal Government: Experience in government regulated compliance environments
  • Technical Skills: Experience with SharePoint administration, and PowerApps development
  • Incident Response: Hands-on incident response experience in regulated environments
  • Verified Experience: Preference for candidates with verified work experience over recent college graduates
  • Emerging technologies: Artificial intelligence (AI), Robotic Process Automation (RPA), Large Language Models (LLM)

JOB SUMMARY:

The Senior Product Manager is responsible for the strategic leadership of a platform, product line, or high-complexity product within the clinical research space. This role defines and owns product vision and roadmap, drives customer-informed strategy, and leads cross-functional execution across one or more significant product domains. The Senior Product Manager operates with a high degree of autonomy, influences senior stakeholders, and serves as a subject matter authority across the product discipline.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES: To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty and responsibility satisfactorily. The accountabilities listed below are representative of the knowledge, skills, and/or ability required.

  • Discovers and validates market problems through:

    • Collaborating closely with internal product stakeholders for market-facing product offerings.

    • Reviewing industry guidelines, specifications, and regulations on an ongoing basis.

    • Interacting with users/buyers of the platform to collect and synthesize product inputs.

    • Meeting with current and potential customers to understand the customer voice.

    • Identifying industry disruptions that are driving spending in the clinical market space.

  • Thoroughly understands customer needs and user centric design to define internal and external customer requirements.

  • Optimizes trade-off decisions during the development process.

  • Provides strategic leadership for the platform or product line, including technical, commercial, and market-facing aspects.

  • Leads the development of AI-embedded product strategies for the assigned platform or product line, defining how AI, machine learning, and advanced analytics capabilities will be prioritized, sequenced, and delivered to drive measurable client value.

  • Develops, maintains, and communicates product vision, positioning, value proposition, buyer/user personas, competitive information, and roadmaps for individual products within a product line.

  • Develops, owns, and maintains roadmap and product vision to gain stakeholder consensus and approval of product initiatives.

  • Owns the overall scoping of product initiatives in conjunction with setting and managing expectations of business leadership, Engineering, and Data teams.

  • Coaches and mentors Product Managers and Associate Product Managers in identifying, scoping, and presenting AI-driven product opportunities, ensuring consistent quality of AI feature development across the team.

  • Contributes to the preparation of statements of work, RFI responses, and marketing collateral.

  • Delivers presentations/demonstrations at customer sites, trade shows, and via web conference.

  • Other duties as assigned by supervisor. These may, on occasion, be unrelated to the position described here.

EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education, skills, and experience to perform the job.

CERTIFICATIONS/LICENSE/REGISTRATION REQUIREMENTS: None

QUALIFICATIONS/EXPERIENCE:

  • Minimum of 5 years of experience in product management, business analysis, or software engineering; experience in clinical research or healthcare technology required.

  • Functional understanding of the broader clinical research process, clinical operations, and/or multiple clinical software systems (e.g., for clinical site support, patient engagement, safety, regulatory review, etc,)

  • Commercial software delivery experience in a 21 CFR Part 11 validated environment is a plus.

  • Demonstrated ability to make rapid and complex decisions that optimize across multiple, and at times, competing objectives.

  • Demonstrated experience incorporating AI, machine learning, or advanced analytics capabilities into product strategy and roadmap decisions, with the ability to evaluate feasibility, articulate client impact, and align AI investments to business objectives.

  • Results orientation, team player and holding self and others accountable for achieving results for customers and the business.

  • Demonstrated ability to operate and influence at the team level in a complex, matrixed environment with the ability to develop product strategies and execute across multiple sets of customers, internal stakeholders, and products.

  • Strong written and oral communication skills with the ability to effectively communicate technical matters to technical and non-technical individuals, and to all levels of management.

  • Strong interpersonal and collaboration skills

  • Experience with Agile software development methodology preferred.
